title: The _ImageJ_ Problem
text: ImageJ software (https://imagej.net/ij/) widely-used image viewing processing software, particularly popular microscopy life sciences. supports TIFF image format (many others). reads TIFF files perfectly, however can sometimes write peculiar way, meaning softwares try read TIFF files written ImageJ, mistakes can made. what: Frames and Channels in TIFF files
title: The _ImageJ_ Problem
text: volumetric image, frames typically different z-slices. time-stack images (.e. video), frame represents time-point. one channel per colour. conventional colour image made 3 colour channels: red, green blue. grayscale (black white) image just one channel. ’s possible acquire two channels (e.g. red blue green), five channels (e.g. infrared, red, green, blue ultraviolet), number , cases seen mostly specialist imaging fields like microscopy.

what: The Peculiarity of ImageJ TIFF files
title: The _ImageJ_ Problem
text: common use TIFFTAG_SAMPLESPERPIXEL record number channels TIFF image, however ImageJ sometimes leaves TIFFTAG_SAMPLESPERPIXEL value 1 instead encodes number channels TIFFTAG_IMAGEDESCRIPTION might look something like"ImageJ=1.51 images=16 channels=2 slices=8". conventional TIFF reader miss channel information (unusual place). ijtiff miss . ’ll see example . Note: peculiar ImageJ-written TIFF files still bona fide TIFF files according TIFF specification. just break common conventions encoding channel information.

title: ijtiff 3.3.0
text: read_tif() read_tags() can read directly -memory raw vector TIFF bytes; write_tif(img, path = NULL) writes memory returns TIFF file raw vector. 12-bit grayscale TIFFs now readable (values returned 0..4095, big-endian packing assumed). Signed-integer TIFFs now read correct negative values (previously warned read unsigned). read_tif() gains convert argument. convert = "force" decodes image via libtiff’s RGBA reader, converting exotic colorspaces (YCbCr, CMYK/separated, CIELab, …) 8-bit RGB() — useful images previously read non-RGB colorspace (JPEG-YCbCr) meaningfully . convert = "auto" (default) preserves existing behaviour every currently-readable image uses RGBA reader fallback images direct decoder parse . convert = "never" disables . write_tif() can write PHOTOMETRIC_RGB images via tags_to_write = list(photometric = "RGB"); default remains BlackIsZero. Supported TIFF metadata (including PhotometricInterpretation) now round-trips read→write automatically.

title: ijtiff 3.3.0
text: photometric now round-trips, image read WhiteIsZero TIFF re-written WhiteIsZero (previously BlackIsZero). Unwritable source photometrics (Palette/CMYK/YCbCr/CIELab/…) silently written unless convert image.

title: ijtiff 3.3.0
text: Fixed stale check caused “Reading … image” message always say “float” regardless true sample format. read_tif()/read_tags() error messages unsupported images now render values correctly (previously va_list misuse garbled numbers). Fixed memory-safety bug reading corrupt/truncated TIFF errored mid-decode leave dangling handle crash (segfault) subsequent read garbage collection. TIFF handle’s state now heap-owned cleaned finalizer, removing latent double-close/use--free.

title: ijtiff 3.2.0
text: write_tif() now uses tags_to_write parameter accepts named list TIFF tags, consolidating support writable tags (previously used individual parameters). Support writing imagedescription TIFF tag (tag 270) OME-TIFF metadata. Automatic metadata preservation: TIFF tags automatically extracted image attributes (e.g., read_tif()) included writing, enabling round-trip editing without metadata loss. Tag name normalization: tag names tags_to_write now case-insensitive ignore hyphens/underscores. Compression bits-per-sample overrides: tags_to_write can now override compression bits_per_sample parameters.
